brief: Goldman's credit floor sizes the AI debt-issuance wave: hyperscalers are on pace for $250bn of 2026 issuance ($230bn already done, versus sub-$20bn in 2024), and the 2027 forecast was just raised to $420bn from $400bn, with 35% of 2027 hyperscaler capex expected to be debt-funded. Hyperscalers are only 40% of this year's $575bn+ global AI-related debt issuance; project-finance and non-hyperscaler AI issuers add the rest, pushing allocators toward diversifying into Banks, Energy and Healthcare. Issuance is shifting shorter-dated (29.9% to 46.4% in the 0-5yr bucket across H1/H2), though hyperscalers aren't rate-sensitive since interest expense is a small share of earnings. The causal chain: this scale of rate-insensitive borrowing raises long-end yields' sensitivity to debt supply and skews overshoot risk higher, reversible only by lower energy vol or emerging growth worries. Separately, AI-adjacent high-yield supply (SoftBank's record $11.14bn OpenAI bond, Paramount Skydance's ~$12.4bn deal) is testing demand as IG spreads-to-yield sit at lows, and AI single-name CDS volumes have exploded +400% YoY. Equity confidence in the capex cycle hinges on Q3 ROIC proof.
